analysis.title: CIO View: US Equities
key_insights: UBS CIO downgrades US equities from Attractive to Neutral. It says the S&P 500 should still reach new highs in coming months, but risk-reward is becoming more balanced.

Several key market drivers shift from accelerating to decelerating growth in 2027: S&P 500 earnings growth, the pace of positive earnings revisions, AI-related capex growth and the ISM Manufacturing Index.

S&P 500 EPS estimates raised to USD 360 in 2026 (+29% growth) and USD 415 in 2027 (+15% growth). The prior estimates were below consensus, and the raise mainly reflects stronger Q3 results and updated Q4 expectations.
S&P 500 June 2027 target lowered to 8,000 from 8,400, and a December 2027 target of 8,200 introduced. The index closed at 7,417 on 16 Nov 2026.

AI monetization is the main question. AI model revenues would need to approach a couple trillion dollars toward the end of the decade to justify the return on AI investment, versus an estimated run rate below USD 200 billion today.

UBS expects the Fed rate-hiking cycle to end in early 2027, which it calls a potential positive catalyst. Inflation trends still need to improve to give confidence that the Fed will not have to move rates into restrictive territory.

Sector changes: financials cut from Attractive to Neutral on slower growth and a less constructive deregulation backdrop. Energy cut from Neutral to Unattractive because incentives to de-escalate the Middle East war outweigh re-escalation prospects.
Attractive sectors are consumer discretionary, health care, industrials and utilities. About 25% of utilities has material exposure to AI power demand.
Positioning advice: favor higher-quality areas, a more active approach, and use rallies to rebalance equity exposure. UBS expects more range-bound trading in 2027.
Scenario targets for December 2027: Goldilocks 9,500 and AI bust 5,500.

sector_views.rationale: Consumer spending should remain resilient. Energy price increases and volatility are manageable unless prices spike to new highs.
No near-term catalyst for negative health care policy, though UBS is watching policy after the US midterm elections. Higher valuations appear warranted.
Favorable ISM Manufacturing readings add confidence in a cyclical manufacturing upcycle, and the sector has exposure to secular themes.
Defensive characteristics offer ballast if growth slows further. About 25% of the sector has material exposure to AI power demand.
Downgraded from Attractive on slower economic growth and a less constructive deregulation backdrop.
Downgraded from Neutral to Unattractive because incentives to de-escalate the Middle East war outweigh prospects for extended re-escalation.

earnings_insights: UBS CIO raised its S&P 500 EPS estimates to USD 360 for 2026 (+29% growth) and USD 415 for 2027 (+15% growth), UBS estimates, not reported figures. The prior estimates were below consensus.

The raise reflects stronger-than-expected Q3 2026 results (already reported) and updated Q4 expectations. S&P 500 earnings growth is expected to decelerate in 2027 versus 2026, and the pace of positive earnings revisions should moderate.

macro_indicators.reading: Rate-hiking cycle expected to end in early 2027
macro_indicators.interpretation: The end of hikes is a potential positive catalyst for stocks, but inflation must improve so that the Fed does not need to move into restrictive territory.

macro_indicators.reading: Favorable readings, expected to stop accelerating
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports a cyclical manufacturing upcycle view for now. The expectation that it stops accelerating is part of the shift to decelerating growth.
The index is below UBS's 8,000 June 2027 target, which implies roughly 8% upside.

macro_indicators.indicator: US GDP growth in upside scenario
macro_indicators.interpretation: The Goldilocks scenario has AI-driven productivity supporting growth at this pace while the Fed eases.

risk_factors: AI monetization may not ramp fast enough to justify the investment, and AI stocks could deflate on low-return concerns and unsustainable commitments by large AI companies.
AI revenue growth may come at the expense of other segments such as labor income or incumbent businesses.
Inflation may fail to improve enough, forcing the Fed into restrictive territory.
Slower growth and a less constructive deregulation backdrop weigh on financials.
Re-escalation of the Russia-Ukraine and Middle East conflicts, high US tariffs with retaliation, and unforeseen events such as systemic cyberattacks.
vol_and_positioning: UBS expects more range-bound trading in 2027 and recommends using rallies to rebalance equity exposure.
geopolitical: The Middle East war: UBS sees incentives to de-escalate outweighing prospects for extended re-escalation.
Russia-Ukraine conflict: a ceasefire is part of the upside scenario, and escalation is part of the downside scenario.
US tariffs: the upside scenario has the effective tariff rate falling below 10%. The downside has the US keeping a high rate after the midterms, with trading partners increasingly retaliating.
The US midterm elections are a watch item for health care policy and the tariff backdrop.

tension_points.bull_case: AI investment spending and adoption exceed expectations, with better revenue growth and productivity gains. This supports a Goldilocks scenario with a December 2027 S&P 500 target of 9,500.
tension_points.bear_case: AI revenues are below USD 200 billion today against the roughly USD 2 trillion needed by the end of the decade. Concerns about low returns and unsustainable AI commitments could deflate AI stocks, with a December 2027 target of 5,500.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AI model revenues failing to grow on a trajectory toward a couple trillion dollars by the end of the decade.
